_README: Character ceilings for always-loaded memory files. Ported from juniper-ml as P5 of
the shared-session-memory plan (juniper-ml notes/JUNIPER_2026-08-18_JUNIPER-ML_SHARED-SESSION-MEMORY-PLAN.md).
Enforced by util/memory_budget_check.py via the standalone 'Memory Budget' job in
ci.yml. CHARACTERS, not bytes -- the shipped Claude Code check compares
content.length.
WHY THE RATE AXIS SHIPS FIRST. juniper-ml's AGENTS.md grew ~20x in six months WHILE
UNDER FOUR ACTIVE CI GATES: every one enforced structure or currency, none enforced
size. A cut without a ceiling is undone in ~44 days, and a ceiling set AFTER a cut
locks in the inflated level. So the ceiling lands first, and the cut comes later.
The ceiling starts at the size on the day the gate landed, so it is satisfiable
immediately and governs only GROWTH. Ratchet it down after each cut with:
python3 util/memory_budget_check.py --ratchet
BUT --ratchet TIGHTENS TO THE EXACT CURRENT SIZE, leaving ZERO headroom, so the very
next author to add one character fails. It SEEDS; it does not tighten gracefully.
After a real cut, prefer a hand-edit to a value with DELIBERATE SLACK sized to this
repo's own measured burn -- see the measurement recorded below, and re-measure rather
than transcribing it.
RAISING a ceiling FAILS the gate. If a raise is genuinely intended, declare it with an
Allow-Ceiling-Raise: <path>  commit trailer -- deliberately NOT the same trailer as
Allow-Budget-Overrun, because an overrun borrows against a ceiling that still stands
while a raise moves it and erases the debt for everyone.
THIS REPO'S DESTINATIONS ARE NOT docs/REFERENCE.md. That line was inherited from the
juniper-ml original and was false here for the whole cut. Canopy relocated to TWO
files, by subject, in two sequential single-destination PRs: documentation-about-
documentation to docs/DOCUMENTATION_OVERVIEW.md (#540), and the remaining reference
material to a new docs/AGENTS_REFERENCE.md (#541). docs/REFERENCE.md keeps its index
role and carries one row per destination.
None of the three is governed, and for the reason the original gave: capping a
destination would penalise exactly the relocation this plan wants, and they are read
on demand rather than always loaded -- which is the entire point.

AGENTS.md._note: Seeded 2026-08-25 at 95,133 chars, the size of AGENTS.md IN THIS REPO on the day the port landed (zero slack; the job shipped ADVISORY for the soak). RAISED 2026-08-26 to 97,133 (+2,000) under an Allow-Ceiling-Raise: AGENTS.md trailer when --advisory was removed (plan P5 step d): the slack is the largest single AGENTS.md-growing commit re-measured here over the 30 days to 2026-08-26 (max 1,982, median 1,982, ~81 chars/day), floored at 2,000 for the fleet-wide fan-out class that added 1,982 chars to six repos' AGENTS.md at once on 2026-08-21. Growth past the ceiling now FAILS the check; Allow-Budget-Overrun: AGENTS.md is the loan. After a cut, lower it by hand to a value with RE-MEASURED slack -- never bare --ratchet, which leaves zero headroom.

_note: P5 step e (the cut): AGENTS.md relocated to docs/AGENTS_REFERENCE.md verbatim. Ceiling lowered 74,418 -> 51,329 (2026-08-30), then TIGHTENED to 48,581 on 2026-09-03 = size 46,167 + 2,414 slack, where slack is max(largest single 30-day growing commit, 2,000 fleet fan-out floor). RE-MEASURED, not carried: this repo's largest single AGENTS.md-growing commit over the 30 days to 2026-09-03 is 2,414 (median 1,982, p90 2,414, ~81 chars/day) -- canopy is the SLOWEST-growing repo in the fleet, not a fast one, and 51,329 left 5,162 of headroom against a 2,414 worst case. The 2,748 of surplus was accretion room the ratchet exists to deny. Set by hand, NOT by --ratchet, which leaves zero headroom and fails the next author on one character.
